title: Trains to Cosford
from: the main stations around the country
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the RAF Cosford Air Show. Cosford has its own little station right by the airfield, and West Midlands Railway stops there once an hour each way on its Birmingham to Shrewsbury trains. That one hourly train is the bit to plan around. I’ve added connections from the big stations that work well too, like Avanti from London Euston, CrossCountry from Leeds and Nottingham, and Transport for Wales from Cardiff and Manchester. Pick your station and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the RAF Cosford Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: Cosford station sits right next to the airfield, so it’s only about 300 metres to the show. On show day there are staff and signs, and honestly you can just follow everyone else. There is no step free route between the platforms, so if you use a wheelchair or struggle with steps, please take a look at the show’s accessibility page before you book.
walkBack: Allow about 10 minutes to walk back to the station, and a lot longer when the flying finishes, as there’s a queue system at the station when it gets busy.
tip: Only one train an hour stops at Cosford each way on a normal Sunday, so I would plan the Cosford train first and work back from it. Missing it by a minute can mean nearly an hour on the platform.
The station gets very busy straight after the flying. I would either leave during a display you’re less bothered about, or stay and look round the stalls, get some food and let the first rush go.

In past years West Midlands Railway has run extra trains after the show, and some Transport for Wales trains that don’t normally stop have called at Cosford. The summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.
alt: When I last checked, an off peak day return from Wolverhampton was £6.20 and from Birmingham New Street £11.00, so the short hops are cheap.

From further away, booking an advance ticket on the long leg can save a lot. If you’re going as a family, a Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, so it may well pay for itself on this one trip.
note: Times are from the National Rail timetable for Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026, so they are a guide to how Sunday trains run rather than the show day times. Sunday times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, and extra trains are often added for the show, so please check before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: West Midlands Railway, plus the connections that work well. Every journey ends on the West Midlands Railway train that stops at Cosford. I’ve only included connections from the big stations where the change is sensible and the whole trip works on a Sunday. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

about.Birmingham New Street|Wolverhampton: Out of New Street through the Black Country, past Smethwick and Sandwell. It’s busy railway, with trains every few minutes.
about.Wolverhampton|Cosford: Out of Wolverhampton the city gives way to fields quickly. You call at Bilbrook, Codsall and Albrighton, and you’ll spot the airfield on your left just before Cosford.
about.Wolverhampton|Shrewsbury: Through the Shropshire countryside, past Cosford and the airfield, then Telford and Wellington with the Wrekin in view.
about.Cosford|Telford Central: A short run through Shifnal and on into Telford.
about.Cosford|Shrewsbury: Through Shifnal, Telford and Wellington. Look out for the Wrekin, the big hill on your left heading west.
about.Telford Central|Cosford: A short run back through Shifnal to Cosford, with the airfield just before the station.
about.Shrewsbury|Cosford: East through Wellington and Telford, with the Wrekin off to the right, then Shifnal and Cosford.
about.Shrewsbury|Telford Central: East through Wellington, with the Wrekin off to the right.
about.London Euston|Birmingham New Street: Up the West Coast Main Line past Watford and Milton Keynes, then through Coventry and Birmingham International.
about.London Euston|Wolverhampton: Up the West Coast Main Line past Milton Keynes and Rugby, through Coventry and Birmingham, and on to Wolverhampton.
about.London Euston|Milton Keynes Central: Out of London through Watford and the Chiltern Hills.
about.Milton Keynes Central|Rugby: Through the Northamptonshire countryside, past the Kilsby tunnel.
about.Coventry|Birmingham New Street: Past Birmingham International, right by Birmingham Airport, so keep an eye out for aircraft on the left.
about.Birmingham New Street|Coventry: Past Birmingham International, right by Birmingham Airport, so keep an eye out for aircraft on the right.
about.Stafford|Wolverhampton: A short run south down the West Coast Main Line through Penkridge.
about.Crewe|Stafford: South down the West Coast Main Line through the Staffordshire countryside.
about.Crewe|Shrewsbury: Through the Cheshire and Shropshire countryside, past Nantwich, Whitchurch and Wem.
about.Manchester Piccadilly|Crewe: South through Stockport and Wilmslow, and on across the Cheshire plain.
about.Manchester Piccadilly|Stockport: Out of Piccadilly and across the big viaduct into Stockport.
about.Stockport|Crewe: South through Wilmslow and across the Cheshire plain.
about.Cardiff Central|Newport: Along the South Wales Main Line into Newport.
about.Newport|Hereford: Up the Welsh Marches line through Abergavenny, with the Black Mountains to the west.
about.Hereford|Shrewsbury: Through Leominster, Ludlow and Church Stretton, with the Long Mynd hills beside you. It’s one of the prettiest lines in the country.
about.Cardiff Central|Shrewsbury: Up the Welsh Marches line through Newport, Abergavenny, Hereford and Ludlow. It’s a lovely run along the border.
about.Leeds|Sheffield: South through Wakefield, with views over the old Yorkshire coalfield.
about.Sheffield|Derby: Through Chesterfield, past the famous crooked spire, and down the Derwent valley.
about.Leeds|Birmingham New Street: The CrossCountry route south through Wakefield, Sheffield and Derby.
about.Derby|Birmingham New Street: Through Burton upon Trent, home of the breweries, and Tamworth.
about.Nottingham|Derby: West along the Trent valley through Beeston and Long Eaton.
about.Nottingham|Birmingham New Street: Through Derby and Burton upon Trent, then Tamworth into Birmingham.
